Lean evidence for the COMPANION program (spec/uniform.json, 7932/10^7; tag CU32, bank B2Gcu32)
==============================================================================================

This is NOT the program this package prices (certificates/gcert1-p10-b325-c2.json.gz, 7940/10^7), whose Lean run is
pending. The companion is the same recipe with one shared PR #325 pair module; its certificate is not in this
package (sha256 below; verify.py regenerates its word only as the builder anchor (f)). It is the Lean-checked counterpart of PR #346's supplier (same coarse saving b).

What this file is. These are the console outputs of the Lean run, copied from the session log of the run
(2026-10-11, host "spark", Ubuntu; a checkout of jacobalansussman/wht-power-saving-lean at commit f010392 with the
Lean toolchain and Mathlib that commit pins, the same commit as PR #327's Lean runs). The generated Lean modules and the full build log stayed
on that host; they are not in this package, and nothing here is re-run by verify.py. The run used Sussman's
generator unchanged. Lines are verbatim; "..." marks omitted lines and [ ] marks notes added here.

Program built: the committed certificate, gz sha256

56e1139aa4a420219d37b9af00d8894d4c21df83b3d9c266d36a787676e9ad4e (the program was emitted under the name
p10-b325-pmqm).


1. Generate the Lean modules (Sussman's tools/gx/regen_check.py, unchanged)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------

      $HOME/cxup/lean/gcert1-p10-b325-pmqm.json.gz CU32 B2Gcu32 --keep $HOME/cxup/lean/gen > ~/cxup/lean/regen.log 2>&1

$ grep -i -m8 "accept\|rate\|1 - \|exponent\|segments" ~/cxup/lean/regen.log

[regen_check.py's own RESULT line compares the generated files with files of the same name committed in Sussman's
 repository. For a new program none exist, so it reports 35 files "not in the repository", 0 different, and prints
 FAIL. That line does not judge the program; the mirror line above ("CU32: mirror accepts") and the Lean build
 below do. PR #327's CC95/CP37 runs and our CX97 run went through the same step.]

$ ls ~/cxup/lean/gen/Work/GCert/Data

2. Kernel-check the solution module
-----------------------------------

$ cd ~/wht-lean && cp -R ~/cxup/lean/gen/Work/GCert/Data/. Work/GCert/Data/
$ lake build Work.GCert.Data.SolutionB2Gcu32x > ~/cxup/lean/build.log 2>&1; echo BUILD_EXIT $? >> ~/cxup/lean/build.log

$ grep -c "error" ~/cxup/lean/build.log; grep BUILD_EXIT ~/cxup/lean/build.log; grep -i "Build completed\|jobs" ~/cxup/lean/build.log | tail -2
0
BUILD_EXIT 0
Build completed successfully (9220 jobs).

$ grep "wht_main_block_B2Gcu32x" ~/cxup/lean/build.log | tail -2
info: Work/GCert/Data/SolutionB2Gcu32x.lean:38:0: 'OAI.PowerSaving.WHT.wht_main_block_B2Gcu32x' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]


3. Compare the solution with the challenge statement (Sussman's tools/Compare.lean)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[The first Compare.lean attempt stopped because the challenge module had not been built yet ("object file ...
 ChallengeB2Gcu32x.olean ... does not exist", CMP_EXIT 1). The challenge module was then built and the comparison
 re-run:]

$ lake build Work.GCert.Data.ChallengeB2Gcu32x 2>&1 | tail -2
warning: Work/GCert/Data/ChallengeB2Gcu32x.lean:323:8: declaration uses `sorry`
Build completed successfully (8924 jobs).

$ lake env lean --run tools/Compare.lean Work.GCert.Data.ChallengeB2Gcu32x Work.GCert.Data.SolutionB2Gcu32x \
      OAI.PowerSaving.WHT.wht_main_block_B2Gcu32x 2>&1 | tail -8
...
  identical: OAI.PowerSaving.WHT.wht   [solution: WHTCheck.Solution]
  identical: OAI.PowerSaving.WHT.whtInKind   [solution: WHTCheck.Solution]
  identical: OAI.PowerSaving.WHT.whtOutKind   [solution: WHTCheck.Solution]
OK: every statement dependency is identical in the solution
solution proof reaches 37839 constants; axioms: #[Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext]
OK: only permitted axioms

RESULT: PASS

[The `sorry` is in the challenge module, which states the theorem without proof (as in Sussman's own challenge
 files); the solution module proves it, and Compare.lean checks that the two statements agree.]


Scope
-----
The theorem is the Walsh-Hadamard power-saving statement of Sussman's repository at exponent 1 - 7932084/10^10,
built from this program with his unchanged generator. It is not an integer-multiplication κ assembly. The official
comparator (landrun sandbox) and a clean build from an empty cache were not run for this program.
